jurisdiction.name: Group of Seven
jurisdiction.overview: Informal forum of seven economies and the EU, with a rotating presidency and no secretariat. Its AI texts are political commitments by Leaders and Ministers.

narrative.summary: Since 2023 the G7 has led the Hiroshima AI Process, adopting guiding principles and a code of conduct for developers of advanced AI, a comprehensive policy framework and, with the OECD, a voluntary reporting framework. Ministers' declarations under the Italian (2024), Canadian (2025) and French (2026) presidencies added an action plan on AI in the world of work, a toolkit for AI in the public sector, measures on AI adoption by small firms and a shared terminology on open AI.
narrative.review_notes: The Hiroshima AI Process site of Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, which publishes the full texts, was searched, and membership is taken from Global Affairs Canada's G7 page. The Friends Group list (69 countries and the EU as of August 2026) is kept as context, since members support 'the spirit' of the process rather than adopting the texts, and later outputs (the March 2024 ministerial declaration and the reporting framework) are pending.

instruments.official_title: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems
instruments.english_title: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems
instruments.current_status: Published in full on the Hiroshima AI Process site of Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, the ministry that led the process for the 2023 Japanese G7 presidency (the G7 has no secretariat). Welcomed by G7 Leaders in the G7 Leaders' Statement on the Hiroshima AI Process of 30 October 2023, to which it is attached; the document itself carries no date, so the date of that statement is used. Leaders 'call on organizations developing advanced AI systems to commit to the application of the International Code of Conduct'. Voluntary for organisations; a political commitment, not legally binding.

instruments.official_title: G7 Leaders' Statement on the Hiroshima AI Process
instruments.english_title: G7 Leaders' Statement on the Hiroshima AI Process
instruments.summary: G7 leaders recognise the opportunities of advanced AI systems, including foundation models and generative AI, and the need to manage their risks. They welcome the Hiroshima Process International Guiding Principles and Code of Conduct for organisations developing advanced AI systems, call on developers to commit to the Code, and instruct ministers to complete a comprehensive policy framework with the OECD and GPAI and a work plan by the end of 2023.
instruments.current_status: Statement of the G7 Leaders, 30 October 2023 (Japan presidency). Political commitment.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF read 2026-10-21; date printed. Also on international.gc.ca/.../g7/documents/2023-10-30-ai-hiroshima-ia.aspx.

instruments.official_title: Hiroshima Process International Guiding Principles for All AI Actors
instruments.english_title: Hiroshima Process International Guiding Principles for All AI Actors
instruments.issuing_authority: G7 Digital and Tech Ministers; endorsed by G7 Leaders
instruments.publisher_name: G7 Digital and Tech Ministers; endorsed by G7 Leaders
instruments.summary: Extends the eleven Hiroshima guiding principles for organisations developing advanced AI systems to all AI actors, as appropriate to their role across the AI lifecycle, covering risk management, incident reporting, transparency, security, content provenance, research and data protection. Adds a twelfth principle on responsible use and digital literacy, including awareness of risks such as disinformation.
instruments.current_status: Part of the Hiroshima AI Process Comprehensive Policy Framework agreed by G7 Digital and Tech Ministers on 1 December 2023 and endorsed by G7 Leaders on 6 December 2023. Non-binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: The PDF prints no date; date is that of the Ministers' Statement of 1 December 2023 (document02_en.pdf, already recorded as the Comprehensive Policy Framework) of which it forms part. If the editor treats it as a component of the existing framework record, merge instead.

instruments.official_title: Ministerial Declaration: The G7 Digital and Tech Ministers' Meeting
instruments.english_title: G7 Digital and Tech Ministers' Declaration, Takasaki (with Annex 5: Action Plan for promoting global interoperability between tools for trustworthy AI)
instruments.summary: Ministerial declaration with a dedicated AI section calling for human-centric, risk-based AI policy grounded in human rights and democratic values, interoperable AI governance frameworks and international technical standards, and an early stocktake of generative AI opportunities and risks. Annex 5 sets an action plan for promoting global interoperability between tools for trustworthy AI.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G7 Digital and Tech Ministers on 30 April 2023 under Japan's presidency. Political commitment.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF on soumu.go.jp read 2026-10-21: date 30 April 2023 printed; no place printed (meeting held in Takasaki, Gunma). AI section paras 39-48; Annex 5.

instruments.official_title: G7 Industry, Technology and Digital Ministerial Declaration (with Annex 3: Advancing the Outcomes of the Hiroshima Artificial Intelligence Process)
instruments.english_title: G7 Industry, Technology and Digital Ministerial Declaration, Verona and Trento (with Annex 3 on advancing the Hiroshima AI Process)
instruments.issuing_authority: G7 Industry, Technology and Digital Ministers
instruments.publisher_name: G7 Industry, Technology and Digital Ministers
instruments.summary: Ministerial declaration whose AI sections call for safe, secure and trustworthy AI, a report on AI adoption by micro, small and medium enterprises, attention to competition in AI markets, and a toolkit for AI in the public sector. Annex 3 commits members to advance the Hiroshima AI Process outcomes, including a monitoring mechanism for voluntary application of the Code of Conduct developed with the OECD and outreach to developing countries.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G7 Industry, Technology and Digital Ministers in March 2024 under Italy's presidency. Political commitment.
instruments.evidence_reference: Text prints no title date; 15 March 2024 is the date printed for it on soumu.go.jp HAIP documents page, and the Italian presidency documents page lists the meeting as 13-15 March. Also at g7italy.it/wp-content/uploads/G7-Industry-Tech-and-Digital-Ministerial-Declaration-Annexes-1.pdf.

instruments.official_title: Towards an Inclusive Human-Centered Approach for New Challenges in the World of Work (G7 Labour and Employment Ministers' Declaration), with Annex 1: G7 Action Plan for a human-centered development and use of safe, secure and trustworthy AI in the World of Work
instruments.english_title: G7 Action Plan for a Human-Centred Development and Use of Safe, Secure and Trustworthy AI in the World of Work (G7 Labour and Employment Ministers' Declaration, Cagliari)
instruments.summary: Labour ministers' declaration with a dedicated section on human-centred AI in the world of work and an annexed action plan. Ministers commit to building on the Hiroshima AI Process and OECD AI Principles, reskilling workers affected by AI and protecting data workers. The action plan sets policy options on skills, monitoring job impacts, privacy and non-discrimination, occupational safety, transparency and human oversight, and social dialogue, and asks the ILO and OECD to report on progress.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G7 Labour and Employment Ministers in Cagliari, 12-13 September 2024, under Italy's presidency. Political commitment.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF read 2026-10-21; prints 'Cagliari, 12-13 September 2024'; date given as last day. Apulia Leaders' Communiqué tasked labour ministers with this action plan.

instruments.official_title: G7 Toolkit for Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector
instruments.english_title: G7 Toolkit for Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector
instruments.issuing_authority: G7 Italian Presidency, prepared by the OECD and UNESCO
instruments.publisher_name: G7 Italian Presidency, prepared by the OECD and UNESCO
instruments.summary: Practical guidance to help governments turn principles for safe, secure and trustworthy AI into public-sector policies. It reviews national AI strategies, governance structures and safeguards, G7 public-sector AI use cases, benefits and implementation challenges, and sets out an implementation journey from framing and ideation through prototyping, piloting and scaling, with monitoring and stakeholder engagement throughout.
instruments.current_status: Prepared by the OECD and UNESCO for the 2024 Italian G7 presidency and launched at the G7 Digital and Technology Ministerial Meeting on 15 October 2024, where ministers welcomed it. Non-binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF read 2026-10-21: (c) OECD/UNESCO 2024; preface by OECD SG, UNESCO DG and Italian Undersecretary Butti; notes it does not necessarily reflect member countries' official views. Date = ministerial meeting date under which the presidency lists it (15 October). Welcomed in Cernobbio Joint Statement.

instruments.official_title: Ministerial Meeting on Technology and Digital: G7 Joint Statement
instruments.english_title: G7 Digital and Technology Ministers' Joint Statement, Cernobbio
instruments.summary: Ministers welcome the G7 Toolkit for AI in the Public Sector, take stock of the OECD pilot of the Hiroshima AI Process reporting framework and set the aim of finalising the framework by year-end, plan a voluntary brand to identify organisations that report under the Code of Conduct, and commit to improving interoperability between AI governance approaches, alongside digital government and digital identity.
instruments.current_status: Joint statement of G7 Digital and Technology Ministers, Cernobbio, 15 October 2024 (Italy presidency). Political commitment.

instruments.english_title: Reporting Framework for the Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems
instruments.issuing_authority: G7, with the OECD (hosted on OECD.AI)
instruments.publisher_name: G7, with the OECD (hosted on OECD.AI)
instruments.summary: Standardised questionnaire through which organisations developing advanced AI systems report voluntarily on how they apply the eleven actions of the Hiroshima Code of Conduct, including risk identification and mitigation, incident reporting, information sharing, security, content authentication and transparency. Reports are published on the OECD.AI site.
instruments.current_status: Launched on 7 February 2025; the G7 agreed the questionnaire and operational procedure with the OECD's co-operation, and the OECD hosts reporting. Participation is voluntary; a second version (Reporting Framework 2.0) has since been used.
instruments.evidence_reference: Launch date from Japan MIC press release 7 Feb 2025 (soumu.go.jp/main_sosiki/joho_tsusin/eng/pressrelease/2025/2/7_3.html): 'with the cooperation of the OECD, the G7 agreed on the questionnaire and the operational procedure'. OECD.AI: 'first launched in February 2025'; questionnaire at oecd.ai/assets/files/haip-reporting-framework-v2.docx (v2). Listed in OECD brief; recorded here under G7 as the agreeing body, cross-referenced as a lead in OECD.json.

instruments.official_title: G7 Leaders' Statement on AI for Prosperity
instruments.english_title: G7 Leaders' Statement on AI for Prosperity
instruments.summary: G7 leaders commit to drive AI adoption in the public sector through a G7 GovAI Grand Challenge and a G7 AI Network, launch a G7 AI Adoption Roadmap to help small and medium-sized enterprises adopt AI, address the energy demands of AI with a workplan due by year-end, and expand AI access for emerging market and developing countries.
instruments.current_status: Statement of G7 Leaders, Kananaskis, 17 June 2025 (Canada presidency). Political commitment.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read on pm.gc.ca 2026-10-21; date and place printed. g7.canada.ca disallows automated fetching.

instruments.official_title: G7 2025 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministerial Declaration
instruments.english_title: G7 2025 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministerial Declaration, Montréal
instruments.issuing_authority: G7 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministers
instruments.publisher_name: G7 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministers
instruments.summary: Ministers set a human-centric approach to secure, responsible and trustworthy AI as a driver of productivity, support SME adoption through the SME AI Adoption Blueprint and a toolkit, back the Hiroshima Code of Conduct reporting framework and ask the OECD to help users understand reports, commit to closing AI talent gaps, and launch the G7 AI Network for public-sector AI using shared open-source solutions.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G7 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministers in Montréal on 9 December 2025 (Canada presidency). Political commitment.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF prints 'Montréal, Canada, December 9, 2025' (soumu listing shows December 10).

instruments.official_title: G7 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministerial Statement on the SME AI Adoption Blueprint
instruments.english_title: G7 Ministerial Statement on the SME AI Adoption Blueprint
instruments.issuing_authority: G7 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministers
instruments.publisher_name: G7 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministers
instruments.summary: Ministers welcome the SME AI Adoption Blueprint developed under Canada's presidency, noting that SMEs adopt AI more slowly than large firms. They set out policy actions on affordable infrastructure, quality datasets, open-source models, AI skills and planning, pooled financing and shared resources, and clear governance guidance suited to SMEs.
instruments.current_status: Statement of G7 Industry, Digital and Technology Ministers, Montréal, 9 December 2025. Political commitment.

instruments.official_title: Déclaration ministérielle du G7 sur le numérique et les technologies
instruments.english_title: G7 Ministerial Declaration on Digital and Technology, Paris
instruments.summary: Ministerial declaration with sections on promoting secure AI (risks, misuse and resilience) and on accelerating AI adoption for growth, including AI openness, SME adoption and an SME AI readiness tool with the OECD. It also addresses the energy and resource demands of AI and generative AI risks to minors, and continues work under the Hiroshima AI Process.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G7 Digital and Technology Ministers in Paris on 29 May 2026 under France's presidency. Political commitment.
instruments.evidence_reference: Text prints 'Paris, 29 May' without year; year from the presidency's page (Elysée G7 Evian article of 1 June 2026: ministers met in Paris on 29 May 2026) and the soumu HAIP listing under 2026. English version: soumu.go.jp/hiroshimaaiprocess/pdf/document12_en.pdf ('G7 Ministerial Declaration on Digital & Technology').

instruments.official_title: Vision du G7 sur les opportunités offertes par une IA ouverte et sur l'établissement d'une terminologie commune
instruments.english_title: G7 Vision on the Opportunities of Open AI and on Establishing a Common Terminology
instruments.summary: G7 ministers set out the economic benefits of open AI and four principles and a tiered typology describing degrees of openness of AI systems, from fully open-source AI with open data to models publishing weights under usage-restricted licences, to give a shared, precise terminology and reduce 'open washing'.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G7 Digital and Technology Ministers at their meeting in Paris on 29 May 2026 under France's presidency. Non-binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF prints no date; text opens 'Nous, ministres du G7 chargés du numérique et des technologies'. Elysée G7 page (1 June 2026) states the common vision on degrees of openness of AI systems was adopted at the 29 May 2026 ministerial meeting. English title is a translation.

leads.title: G7 Evian: 'Appel des chefs d'État et de gouvernement pour un espace numérique plus sûr pour les mineurs' (published 17 June 2026)
leads.note: Official text on the French presidency's G7 Evian site (elysee.fr); supported by Brazil, Egypt, India, Kenya and Korea.
